app.title: Alias Workbench
app.readonlyNote: the dry run shows every object beforehand. Without it nothing is written.
tree.noObjectHint: no object — derived from the ID only
result.header: What the type-detector makes of it
result.pickSomething: Pick a channel, device or folder on the left.
result.noObject: There is no object for this node.
result.noObjectText: MQTT only creates objects for the datapoints themselves, not for the levels above. The type-detector needs a channel or device — which is exactly why you build an alias. The points below are all there and usable as sources.
result.tooManyStates: That would be a device with {0} states — usually this means the wrong node is selected. In the tree on the left, nodes that look like a single device carry a dot. You can still build it this way.
pattern.label: Pattern
pattern.noPlaceLong: no slot in the {0} pattern — the point is still created and fully usable, only Alexa and friends count it separately
target.name: Name
target.folderHint: separate subfolders with a dot, e.g. House.GF.Kitchen
tpl.label: Template
tpl.forcedHint: Detection does not trigger for this template — chosen by hand.
tpl.nameHint: name matches "{0}" — not detectable from MQTT
tpl.noNameHint: the name gives no hint — "{0}" is the default, from MQTT they are indistinguishable
list.onlyInDevice: only what belongs to the device
detail.name: Name
detail.separateHint: separate — the switch shows the state, not the command
detail.formulaHint: "ON"/"OFF" → boolean is done by the alias itself, no formula needed.
detail.writeFormulaHint: converts the other way: what the device should receive when switched.
detail.caption: Caption
info.sameDatapoints: {0} — the same datapoints, only sorted differently.
info.explain: They stay where they are and are perfectly usable in VIS, scripts and InfluxDB. The {0} pattern has no slot for them, so the detector groups them as a second device called info. This is only visible where devices are listed — Material, Alexa, Google, HomeKit.
folder.nothingHere: There is nothing here that could become a device.
folder.clickHint: Click a device to work on it.
folder.clickHintText: A node counts as a device as soon as a template matches it — below that nothing is searched. Where none matches, the node still appears in the list as soon as it has datapoints of its own.
diff.deselectedWithPlace: deselected — would have a slot in the {0} pattern
diff.deselectedNoPlace: deselected — would have no slot in the {0} pattern anyway
check.title: Checks — always running, never touching anything
write.dryTitleCreate: Create alias — this is what would appear
write.dryTitleUpdate: Update alias — this is what would appear
write.removeHint: exist in the alias but no longer appear in the draft
write.noneSelected: Not a single datapoint is selected.
tpl.rememberedHint: This alias was built from this template — it stays until you change it deliberately.
tpls.title: Save as template — {0}
tpls.shadowsPackage: will then shadow the shipped one
tpls.saveAsNewHint: the existing one stays as it is
tpls.head: Header
tpls.nameHintHelp: Only breaks ties between templates that fit equally well — light versus socket, for instance. Separate words with |. This device is called "{0}".
tpls.absoluteTitle: One point refers to a fixed object.
tpls.absoluteText: It does not live under the device and will therefore be the same for every device. Sometimes that is exactly right — a shared setpoint, say. It does not count towards detection.
tpls.contentHelp: Makes detection more precise — and excludes devices that do not send that block. This is exactly what separates "socket" from "socket with metering".
tpls.noRequired: No point is ticked as required — the template would match nothing at all.
tpls.noHits: Matches no device right now. Check the required points.
tpls.savedWhere: It lives in the instance configuration ({0}) and is therefore part of the backup.
tv.paneHead: The template and what it catches
tv.pickTemplate: Pick a template on the left.
tv.packageText: It cannot be edited, so it always stays the state it was delivered in. Duplicate makes a copy of your own, and that copy shadows the original.
tv.importReplaces: Saving replaces your template "{0}" — version {1} becomes version {2}.
tv.importBad: This file is not a template.
tv.badNotObject: A single template as a JSON object is expected.
tv.badState: {0} datapoints without a name or without a read path.
tv.multi: several outputs, one channel {0} per output
tv.nameHintShort: Only breaks ties between templates that fit equally well. Separate words with |.
tv.deleteHint: If it shadows a shipped template, that one reappears afterwards.
tv.rankOwn: The rank only decides between your own templates. Against a shipped one yours always wins anyway — it needs no high rank for that.
tv.rankPackage: The rank only decides between shipped templates, and even there only once evidence and name hint come out even.
tpls.multipleHelp: The {0} in the paths is replaced by %N% — only at the end of a segment, so ENERGY.Power stays intact.
tpls.multipleNoNumber: Enter which number in the paths is the output. Without it the template stays a single one.
tpls.multipleOff: A device with POWER1, POWER2 … becomes a folder with one channel per output.
tv.forbiddenHelp: These points must NOT be present on the device, otherwise the template does not match. This is what separates a single socket from a multi one. Separate several with commas. Absent points do not count as evidence.
tpls.otherOutputsText: A template for several outputs always describes just one — the rest are derived from it. Deselect the foreign points on the device, otherwise the template will only ever fit this one device.
tpls.statesHelp: The left tick says whether the point goes into the template at all. “Default” is the state it will be proposed with on the next device — that comes from your selection on the device. The right tick says whether it must be present for the template to match at all.
tpls.someOff: Deselected on the device: {0}. These points come along as “default off” — on the next device they will be listed, just not ticked.
tpls.loadFailedHint: The instance configuration did not answer in time. Your own templates are not gone — they are only missing from this view. Reload the page.
tv.requiredHelp: These datapoints must be present on the device, otherwise the template does not match. Separate several with commas. Every required point makes the template more precise and more brittle at the same time.
tv.stateHelp: Paths are relative to the device; with "fixed object" it is the full object id. A field from JSON becomes JSON.parse(val).<field> when applied — field and read function are mutually exclusive.
tv.clickRow: Click a row to edit the datapoint
tv.flagsHelp: "Default" = pre-ticked on the next device. "must exist" = without this point the template does not match at all — it moves into the required list above. "fixed object" = the read path is not relative to the device but a full object id, the same for every device.
pattern.slotName: This point sits in slot "{0}" of the {1} pattern. Slot names come from the type-detector and are the same everywhere — they are not translated, because the alias datapoint is named exactly that.
mq.title: MQTT device
mq.nothingYet: The device has not sent anything yet that commands could be read from. "Request status 11" asks for it.
mq.askHint: sends a plain query to the device — it switches nothing and changes no setting
mq.repairHint: These points exist but are not allowed to send. An alias switching through them does nothing, and nothing about it shows.
mq.doneHint: Detection runs again in a moment — a template that did not match before can match now.
